claims.text: Structural stability of multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticles is governed by an interplay among configurational entropy, lattice distortion, and chemical disorder.
Temperature and oxygen partial pressure can be used to alter phase stability.
Composition can be varied to tune nanoparticle structural stability.
The proposed starting material is an as-synthesized multi-element, near-equiatomic solid-solution nanoparticle.
Temperature, oxygen partial pressure, and composition will be varied as the intervention.
The relevant catalytic service range is 773–1173 K.
The relevant thermoelectric service range is 473–1923 K.
Lattice distortion and chemical disorder mediate the response of structural stability to the intervention.
Configurational entropy and lattice distortion influence nanoparticle stability.
Controlled variation of temperature, oxygen partial pressure, and composition will improve structural stability and reduce degradation under service conditions.
The baseline is as-synthesized nanoparticles without controlled variation of temperature, oxygen partial pressure, or composition.
The hypothesis is bounded to 773–1173 K and an oxygen partial pressure of 10^-5–10^-2 atm.
Failure of structural stability to improve under variation of temperature, oxygen partial pressure, and composition would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The conditions include thermoelectric operation over 473–1923 K, but the stated boundary restricts the hypothesis to 773–1173 K, leaving much of the asserted thermoelectric regime outside the hypothesis.
